target.statement: Simple-OPD (LoRA warm-up on teacher CoT + standard OPD) raises the in-domain average on AIME24/AIME25 to 39.69 for a Qwen3-1.7B non-thinking student distilled from a GRPO-trained Qwen3-4B teacher, versus 38.34 for direct OPD (+1.35).
target.table_ref: Table 1, vanilla OPD block, 'Simple-OPD' row, ID Avg column
target.dataset: AIME24 + AIME25 (in-domain eval); warm-up/OPD prompts from DAPO-Math-17K

compute.basis: The target cell requires the full pipeline — regenerate teacher CoT rollouts (Qwen3-4B teacher), LoRA SFT warm-up to saturation (~150-175 steps), then ~300 OPD steps with 128-prompt batches generating up to 8192-token on-policy rollouts under verl+vLLM, plus avg@16 AIME evaluation; on an 8-core CPU with no GPU, 1.7B-token-level rollout generation is prohibitively slow (paper itself uses 8 GPUs), putting this far outside a few CPU-hours.

blockers: No GPU: OPD training (student rollouts + teacher token-level supervision) on 1.7B/4B models is effectively infeasible on 8 CPU cores / 16 GB RAM
Paper's experiments run on eight GPUs; 300 OPD steps with 8192-token rollouts and global batch 128
Needs the RL/GRPO-trained teacher checkpoints (Qwen3-4B GRPO on DAPO-Math-17K; Qwen3-8B+DAPO for Sec. 3), whose public release is unclear
Requires reproducing the teacher's CoT rollout generation and the LoRA-near-saturation warm-up recipe (exact step count matters, 150 vs 175 differ)
Full training stack (verl + vLLM) plus OpenCompass/LMDeploy eval harness needed end-to-end
title: Simple-OPD: Demystifying Warm-up for On-policy Distillation
